recommendations.regimenLabel: Acute pulmonary oedema — IV diuretic ± nitrate + oxygen/NIV
steps: Acute pulmonary oedema: sit up, high-flow O2, IV loop diuretic (furosemide), IV nitrate if hypertensive.
Consider CPAP/NIV for severe respiratory distress.
Daily weights, fluid/salt restriction, monitor renal function and potassium.
Chronic HFrEF: ACEi/ARNI + beta-blocker + MRA + SGLT2 inhibitor.

drugRefs.dose: 40–80 mg IV (or at least equal to the usual oral dose)
drugRefs.freq: repeat/infusion titrated to diuresis and symptoms
drugRefs.why: Rapidly offloads pulmonary congestion in acute decompensation; monitor renal function and potassium.

drugRefs.dose: 10–200 micrograms/min IV infusion, titrated to BP
drugRefs.freq: continuous, titrated to blood pressure and symptoms
drugRefs.why: Venodilatation reduces preload/afterload in hypertensive acute pulmonary oedema; avoid if hypotensive.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Heart Failure and Cor Pulmonale
ESC Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Acute and Chronic Heart Failure
NICE NG106 — Chronic Heart Failure in Adults

drugRefs.dose: start 1.25–2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg/day (or switch to sacubitril/valsartan)
drugRefs.why: Prognostic RAAS blockade in HFrEF; an ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) is preferred where tolerated.

drugRefs.dose: start 1.25 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg/day
drugRefs.why: Reduces mortality in stable HFrEF; up-titrate slowly when euvolaemic.

drugRefs.dose: 25 mg once daily, up to 50 mg/day
drugRefs.why: Prognostic MRA in HFrEF; monitor potassium and renal function.
Reduces heart-failure hospitalisation and mortality across the ejection-fraction spectrum.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Heart Failure and Cor Pulmonale
ESC Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Acute and Chronic Heart Failure
NICE NG106 — Chronic Heart Failure in Adults

decision.label: Acute pulmonary oedema — IV diuretic ± nitrate; NIV if severe

confirm: Dyspnoea, orthopnoea, raised JVP, basal crackles, oedema; raised BNP/NT-proBNP; echo for ejection fraction.
disposition: Admit; ICU/HDU if cardiogenic shock or NIV.
